chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Jibreel informed me of a matter by which my eyes were delighted and my heart was gladdened. He said: O Muhammad! Whoever from your community fights a military campaign in the way of God — no drop of rain from the sky or headache afflicts him except that it will be for him a (status of) martyrdom on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.سَبِيلُ اللَّهِ: The way/path of God — a Quranic phrase for divinely ordained struggle and righteous striving
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Martyrdom or testimony — here indicating that the rank of martyr is granted for all hardships endured in jihad
key_terms.غَزَاة: A military campaign or expedition — specifically in the context of jihad for God's cause
key_terms.قَرَّتْ عَيْنِي: My eyes were cooled/delighted — an Arabic idiom expressing deep joy and contentment

ai.seo_question: What reward does a Muslim fighter receive for hardships suffered during jihad in the way of God?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a hadith from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), who in turn relates a message from the Angel Jibreel: every hardship — however small, even a raindrop or headache — suffered by one who fights in the way of God counts as martyrdom testimony on the Day of Judgment. This teaching was directed at the early Muslim community to encourage perseverance in jihad, assuring fighters that God recognizes and rewards every form of suffering, not only death in battle.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Abu Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> informed me<sup>saww</sup> with such a matter, my<sup>saww</sup> eyes were delighted by it, and my<sup>saww</sup> heart was happy by it. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! The one from your<sup>saww</sup> community who battles is a battle in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so no drop would hit him from the sky or a headache except that there would be (status of) martyrdom for him on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from abu al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘

Jibril informed me of something and it brought delightfulness to my eyes and happiness to my heart. He said, “O Muhammad, anyone of your followers who fights the enemy for the cause of Allah, even if a drop of rain falls on him from the sky or he experiences a headache, he will, on the Day of Judgment, receive for it a reward equal to that for martyrdom.’””
